paper.title: Language Models can Solve Computer Tasks
paper.central_claim: A pre-trained LLM prompted with Recursive Criticism and Improvement (RCI) over task, state and agent grounding can execute MiniWoB++ computer tasks from 2-3 demonstrations, outperforming prior LLM, SL and RL approaches (second to CC-Net SL+RL), and RCI also improves LLM reasoning when external feedback is given.

provenance.independence_note: Aggregation over two seat inputs; the fixed paper text was read before seat scores, but this is not a third blind review or human gold. All results are author reports; nothing was reproduced.

preliminary_evidence_judgment: Read before seat scores. RCI prompts gpt-3.5/gpt-4 to plan, critique the plan once (explicit RCI), ground the action in current HTML (implicit RCI) and repair format with up to 3 regex-checked retries. MiniWoB++ success is the environment reward (executable), on 55 hand-selected tasks (long-HTML tasks excluded, some tasks modified), with 2-3 task-specific demonstrations, per-task GPT-4 substitution in a separate column, baselines copied from prior papers, no episode counts or variance. Stage ablations on 9 tasks chosen by own success remove whole stages rather than only the critique. The reasoning-benchmark gains stop the RCI loop with the ground-truth label (oracle); Table 17 shows no gain without it. Lineage (ReAct, Reflexion, Self-Refine, WebN-T5, CC-Net) is explicitly discussed in App B.

signatures.object: Per-step action generation of an LLM agent on MiniWoB++: plan -> task-grounded action -> state-grounded action -> agent-grounded action.
signatures.information: Task text, HTML state, plan, history of executed instructions, agent specification (5 regexes); GPT-3/3.5/4 via API; temperature 0, 256 max tokens.
signatures.operation: Explicit RCI on the plan (1 pass); implicit RCI to ground the action to the current HTML (1 pass); implicit RCI to fix format until it matches the regexes (<=3 loops).
signatures.output: One natural-language instruction executed by an instruction-following agent.
signatures.conditions: HTML short enough for context; 2-3 hand-built demonstrations per task.
signatures.feedback: Regex admissibility check (mechanical); otherwise self-critique with no external verdict.
signatures.selection_rule: No candidate selection; each revision replaces the previous output.
signatures.persistence: not_applicable beyond the episode: the plan acts as in-episode memory; nothing persisted across tasks.
signatures.later_use: plan and history used at later steps of the same episode only
signatures.claimed_effect: MiniWoB++ average success above SL/RL SotA aggregates and second only to CC-Net SL+RL with 120x-11,000x fewer samples.
signatures.failure_boundary: Long-horizon, multi-step reasoning, visually rendered tasks (E026); long HTML (E009).

signatures.object: RCI prompting for reasoning benchmarks (8 datasets).
signatures.information: Question plus the ground-truth label as stop signal for up to two RCI loops.
signatures.operation: Criticize previous answer then improve it.
signatures.conditions: Oracle stop signal; without it accuracy <= zero-shot (E018).
signatures.selection_rule: Stop loop when output matches the label.
signatures.claimed_effect: Zero-shot + RCI above zero-shot and CoT on most benchmarks.

gap.author_gap: LLM agents that take keyboard/mouse actions lag behind SL/RL approaches, which need large demonstration sets and task-specific reward functions that are impractical for new tasks.
gap.checked_gap: Real and sourced: trained agents need 12K-2.4M demonstrations (CC-Net, WebN-T5). The paper does not show that the residual limitation of prompted LLM agents lies in grounding rather than raw model strength; the three-stage split is argued by construction.
lineage: WebN-T5-3B / Gur et al. 2022 (LLM fine-tuned on 12K demonstrations), cited
ReAct, Reflexion, Self-Refine, SayCan, Inner Monologue as reasoning/grounding neighbours, cited in App B
gap.lineage_note: The 14-paper references.json has no pre-2023 neighbour; later pinned items (Mind2Web 2306.06070, WebArena 2307.13854) are current_relevance, not ancestors. Lineage statements are author_report from App B.
gap.closest_adjacent: ReAct (interleaved reasoning+action) and Self-Refine/Reflexion (self-feedback refinement); the paper asserts novelty as implicit-feedback self-critique but does not compare to them in the same harness.
gap.residue: Long-horizon planning, multi-step reasoning, vision-dependent tasks, long HTML, action space limited to click/type.
gap.stakes: Practical few-shot computer-control without reward engineering (author claim).
gap.method_response: Inference-time critique loops at three grounding stages give a model-only substitute for trained grounding components; admissibility is checked by regex.
gap.remaining_gap: Not shown: gains over ReAct/CoT/Self-Refine under the same harness; behaviour outside MiniWoB++.
unresolved: Contribution of RCI vs stronger backbone (gpt-3.5/4 vs T5-3B baseline)
gap.aggregate_neighbor_check: Pinned ReAct (2210.03629) predates RCI and is named by RCI as closest; RCI's stated residual is implicit (label-free) critique plus three grounding stages. For the computer-task claim this residual is coherent; for the reasoning claim it is undercut by the paper's own label-stopping protocol.
